key_insight: Quantum Density Functional Theory reduces the qubit requirement for an N-orbital Kohn–Sham simulation to O(log₂ N), with an experimental demonstration for lithium hydride.
engineering_relevance: Pairing qubit-efficient algorithms with programmable integrated photonics offers a route toward lower-resource quantum chemistry simulations.
method: Reformulate interacting electrons using a non-interacting Kohn–Sham reference system.
Use an ensemble variational quantum eigensolver over the ground- and first-excited-state subspace.
Execute on a programmable photonic circuit fed by a deterministic quantum-dot single-photon source.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experimental evaluation of LiH ground- and first-excited-state properties, but provides no numerical accuracy or hardware-performance metrics.
watch_item: Logarithmic qubit scaling does not establish comparable reductions in total computational cost or accuracy for larger molecules.
paper_title: Quantum Simulation of Electronic Structure using Quantum Density Functional Theory on a Programmable Integrated Photonic Circuit
